The `// other cases?` comment signals that the cancellation-during-reduce test only asserts on `MultiBucketsAggregation` results and silently passes for all other aggregation types (e.g. metrics, matrix stats). If a non-multi-bucket aggregation type also returns early before reaching the cancellation check, the test will pass without verifying anything. Consider either:
- Adding a comment that explicitly documents which aggregation types are expected to return early, or
- Broadening the assertion (e.g. checking that the result is "empty" in a type-appropriate way) so the test actually validates behavior for all aggregation types.

In `testTerms`, the success-path assertion `assertMap("not expected to finish", response, matchesMap())` will always fail when the search completes (the response will contain `took`, `hits`, etc.), which is the intended "fail if it finishes" pattern. However, a bare `fail("Search completed but was expected to time out")` would produce a clearer failure message and make the intent more immediately obvious to someone reading the test, without relying on the reader to understand that `matchesMap()` (empty map) is being used as a sentinel.

The interface name `AggregationcContextSupplier` contains a typo — the `c` in "Aggregationc" should be uppercase `C` to read `AggregationContextSupplier`. Since this is a `public` functional interface in the test framework, the misspelling will be visible to every consumer of the framework and will be harder to fix later (it's a public API name).
